attribution: The signed S has ||S||_2 = 8.31 >> rho(S) = 1 (non-normality gap 7.31). The unsigned |S| is nearly identical (||.||_2 = 8.32, rho = 1), so on the FULL graph the SIGNS barely move either quantity. The symmetrized (S+S^T)/2 is normal, so its 2-norm equals its spectral radius (gap 0): removing the DIRECTEDNESS removes the non-normality entirely. The 8.31-vs-1 phenomenon is therefore directedness-driven non-normality, not a sign effect. (The signed spectral radius only drops below 1 on small frustrated SUBGRAPHS, see tests/test_propagation.py; on the full graph it stays 1. The symmetrized rho = 4.18 exceeds 1 because (S+S^T)/2 is no longer a row-stochastic transition.)
